Console.indexTroubleshootingTitle: How to recover and rebuild after indexing fails
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepFix: First fix the reported server, provider balance/key, quota, repository file count/size, or network problem.
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepRestart: Have an indexing client that can read the repository reinitialize its repository session and start a new sync. If it has no manual retry action, reconnect that repository session.
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepKeepOpen: Keep the repository readable by the indexing client while it scans and uploads again. Large repositories take longer.
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepCheck: Use the client’s index-status capability or this page to confirm a new “Indexing” state followed by “Index ready”.
Console.indexTroubleshootingRetryNote: A job marked failed or heartbeat timed out is terminal. Another natural-language question or a console refresh is not a reliable whole-job retry; after fixing the cause, a repository-reading client must create a new sync.
Console.indexTroubleshootingCleanupNote: “Clear failure” removes only failed jobs and staging data. “Delete cloud index” removes the searchable snapshot and requires a full rebuild.
Console.indexFailureEmbeddingInputRejected: Embedding request was rejected by the model service
Console.indexFailureUpstreamBadGateway: Remote indexing service is temporarily unavailable (502)
Console.indexFailureProviderBilling: Upstream model service balance or billing error
Console.indexFailureRepositoryFileLimit: Repository exceeds the indexing file-count limit currently configured by the service
Console.indexFailureRepositoryFileSizeLimit: Repository contains a file above the indexing limit currently configured by the service
Console.indexFailureNetworkUnavailable: Client or server network connection was interrupted
Console.indexRecoveryRestartClient: Check the network and indexing client process. After recovery, have a client that can read the repository reinitialize the repository session and create a new sync while retaining project access.
Console.indexRecoveryResetRoot: This cloud root uses the previous embedding space and cannot accept new writes. Select “Reset cloud index” to delete the repository/branch cloud root and Relay state, then restart the MCP client to rebuild it. Clearing only the failure record will not fix this error.
Console.indexRecoveryFixEmbeddingInput: The model service returned a generic HTTP 400; this does not prove the source file is invalid UTF-8. Verify the generated batch request first. If an exact replay succeeds, restart the MCP client to retry; if it repeats, inspect deployed request serialization and model configuration. Clearing the failure record does not resend the request.
Console.indexRecoveryServiceRecovers: This is a remote index service or gateway failure. When service recovers, reload the repository workspace in its MCP host or restart the LCE MCP client to start a new job.
Console.indexRecoveryFixProviderBilling: Top up the affected model service balance or switch to a working model configuration. Verify it, then restart the MCP client.
Console.indexRecoveryRetryLater: Wait for the provider rate-limit window, reduce concurrency if needed, then restart the MCP client to index again.
Console.indexRecoveryReduceRepository: Ignore generated files, dependencies, and large files, or split the repository to meet file-count and per-file size limits, then restart the MCP client.
Console.indexRecoveryWaitForQuotaReset: A current indexing client that remains running automatically creates a new sync after the server quota resets. If the client is closed or does not support automatic recovery, restart it after quota becomes available.
Console.indexRecoveryFixCredentials: Check the provider URL, API key, and model names. Fix and verify them, then restart the MCP client.
Console.indexRecoveryInspectLogs: Expand the raw error and correlate it with request logs. Fix the root cause and restart the MCP client; do not only clear the record.
